probe:routine: Where do you usually spend your time?
Where might I find you around the house?
probe:house: What can you tell me about this place?
How long have you lived here?
What's the history of this house?
probe:adrian: What do you know about me... before?
Can you tell me who I was?
What was I like before the accident?
probe:crash: Do you know how the accident happened?
comfort: Thank you for your patience with me.
It means a lot that you're helping.
press: I need you to be straight with me.
Stop dodging. Tell me the truth.
You're hiding something. What is it?
leave: I'll let you get back to things.
Excuse me, I need to check something.

marika: I... I don't want to upset you. Not now, Adrian.
Can we talk about something else? Please?
You're pushing too hard. I'm just trying to protect you.
elise: That is not your concern right now.
You need to focus on resting, Adrian. Not interrogating me.
I'd rather not discuss that with you.
vance: I'm not at liberty to discuss that.
That falls outside my medical remit, Adrian.
Let's focus on your physical recovery for now.
hargrove: I'm afraid that's not my place to say, young master.
Perhaps another time, sir. Duties call.
Some family matters are best left undisturbed.
odile: I... I wouldn't know about such things, sir.
It's not my place to speak on that, sir.
I only keep to my cleaning, sir.

routine_claim_lines.marika: I wait by the gate in the morning and evening. In the afternoon I sometimes sit quietly in the parlor.
routine_claim_lines.elise: I spend mornings upstairs, afternoons in the study attending to father's affairs, and evenings upstairs.
routine_claim_lines.vance: Mornings and afternoons I attend to medications upstairs. Evenings I take tea in the kitchen.
routine_claim_lines.hargrove: Mornings I oversee the kitchen, afternoons I attend to the parlor, and evenings I return to the kitchen.
routine_claim_lines.odile: I dust the parlor in the morning, prepare linens in the kitchen in the afternoon, and tend parlor hearths in the evening.

marika: This house has always felt cold to me. Elise never wanted me past the threshold.
Your parents were very proud of this estate, though they rarely invited outsiders.
The gardens by the gate are overgrown, but they're the only place where I feel free.
elise: Our family has held this manor for three generations. Every hallway holds our history.
Father kept his ledgers in the study. Mother spent her hours arranging flowers in the parlor.
Since the crash, the halls echo too loudly. There are too many empty rooms.
vance: Old houses like this harbor dampness and drafts. It isn't ideal for your convalescence.
Elise hired me strictly through an agency. I keep to the upper guest rooms mostly.
The layout is sprawling. One could walk from the kitchen to the study without crossing a soul.
hargrove: I have served your family since you were in swaddling clothes, young master.
Your late father and I would discuss estate upkeep in the study every Thursday evening.
The manor demands constant vigilance. Windows to latch, fires to tend, silver to count.
odile: I have cleaned these rooms twelve years now, sir. Ever since I arrived from the village.
The walls are thick stone, but sound travels strangely through the floorboards at night.
Mistress was very particular about dust behind the library bookcases in the study.

marika: You were gentle, Adrian. You loved sketching near the shore, even in winter.
Before the crash, you promised we would leave this valley together. You bought two tickets.
You had such a quiet laugh. Seeing you look at me like a stranger breaks my heart.
elise: You were always stubborn, Adrian. You argued with father constantly over his investments.
When we were children, you'd hide in the pantry to read adventure novels past midnight.
You promised me you would never leave the family. Then you brought her here.
vance: Your hospital chart indicated extensive cranial contusion. Retrograde amnesia is standard.
You were athletic before the injury, judging from muscle tone. Recovery is largely neurological.
Patients often feel disoriented when familiar faces fail to spark recollection. Give it time.
hargrove: You had your mother's kindness and your father's sharp eye, young master.
I recall teaching you how to hold a fountain pen at the study desk when you were eight.
You were never one for idle gossip. You always preferred deeds to words.
odile: You were always polite to the staff, sir. You never raised your voice like the old master.
You used to leave your pocket watch on the kitchen counter whenever you made midnight tea.
Forgive me, sir, but you look so pale compared to before the accident.

crash_vague.marika: It was a dreadful accident on the winding pass. The authorities said rain caused the skid.
crash_vague.elise: The police called it a tragic collision in the fog. Father lost control on the gorge curve.
crash_vague.vance: The emergency report noted trauma consistent with a severe vehicular impact against the ravine barrier.
crash_vague.hargrove: A horrific accident on the mountain road, young master. The carriage road was slick with rain.
crash_vague.odile: Such a sorrowful crash, sir. The vehicle overturned into the gulley during the squall.

brakes_cut.marika: Everyone knows the brake lines were cut before father even started down the pass.
brakes_cut.elise: Whoever severed the brake cables knew father would never survive that steep descent.
brakes_cut.vance: The mechanic's inspection clearly proved the brake fluid lines were sliced through.
brakes_cut.hargrove: It was foul play, young master; the brake lines had been cut clean through with shears.
brakes_cut.odile: I heard the mechanic whisper that someone cut the brake lines beneath the carriage.

drugged_driver.marika: Father never lost control on that road—his evening drink was drugged with sleeping drops.
drugged_driver.elise: Father wasn't careless; someone placed a heavy sedative drug in his drink before he took the wheel.
drugged_driver.vance: The post-mortem blood analysis detected a concentrated sedative drug in the driver's drink.
drugged_driver.hargrove: The master was sober as a judge, yet someone laced his drink with a toxic drug that night.
drugged_driver.odile: They say the master's drink had a sleeping drug stirred in before he departed in the car.

forced_off_road.marika: It wasn't a solo spin—another car ran them off the road into the ravine.
forced_off_road.elise: Father didn't simply veer off; another car forced them off the road into the rocks.
forced_off_road.vance: The paint scrapes on the rear bumper confirmed another car ran them off the road.
forced_off_road.hargrove: There were foreign tire treads at the crest, young master; another car ran them off the road.
forced_off_road.odile: A delivery boy saw headlights following close—another car ran them off the road into the ditch.

killer.inheritance: A forged last will and testament hidden in the drawer lining, naming the killer as sole beneficiary of the manor estate.
killer.cover_up: Altered clinic records and a concealed amber vial of concentrated chloral hydrate sedative.
killer.obsession: A locked tin of personal photographs of Adrian, with every other family face scratched violently away.

decoy.lingering: Muddy footprints and a damp wool blanket tucked beneath the stone bench by the gate.
decoy.unsent_letters: A packet of tear-stained letters addressed to the late parents, written in Marika's handwriting.
decoy.night_visits: A pair of embroidered slippers by Adrian's door, beside a scrap of paper reading 'is he breathing?'.
decoy.diary: A torn journal page in Elise's hurried hand: 'I want to run away. The walls are closing in.'
decoy.phone_calls: Nurse Vance's handwritten ledger detailing repeated midnight trunk calls to an unlisted city bureau.
decoy.skimming_pills: Blister strips of prescription sleeping capsules concealed inside an empty tea canister.
decoy.pawned_watch: A pawn broker's receipt from the capital pawnshop for a gold pocket watch bearing the Hargrove initials.
decoy.drinking: An opened bottle of rye whiskey secreted behind dry sacks in the back of the pantry.
decoy.stolen_silver: An ornate heirloom silver soup ladle rolled tightly inside an apron in the linen press.
decoy.eavesdropping: A thin tumbler glass resting upside down on the hallway floorboard outside the study door.

world.official_report: The coroner's preliminary report: 'Vehicle damage extensive. Exact mechanical status undetermined pending forensic laboratory review.'
world.hospital_letter: Discharge documentation from St. Jude's Trauma Center: 'Patient Adrian suffered cranial trauma following road collision on October 1st.'

hargrove.sound: You hear a slow pocket-watch tick.
hargrove.sight: A white cuff on a dark sleeve.

vance.sound: A wristwatch tick and squeaking soles.
vance.sight: A white cuff on a grey sleeve.

elise.sight: A ribbon trailing in the dark.

marika.sight: Long pale-gold hair falling across your face.

odile.sight: A white lace cap in the dark.

search_blocked: {name} is present in the room, watching your every movement. You cannot search without drawing suspicion.
search_nothing: You search through drawers and shelves, but uncover nothing out of the ordinary here.

inheritance.marika: Marika falls to her knees, trembling: 'The will was forged before you ever returned. I thought if you and Elise were gone, everything would finally be mine. I'm sorry... I'm so sorry.'
inheritance.elise: Elise stares cold and unblinking down the barrel: 'This house was meant for me alone. Father was going to disinherit us both for his charity foundations. I protected what is mine.'
inheritance.vance: Nurse Vance drops her clinical facade, exhaling sharply: 'The will named my silent partners. A tidy sum for ensuring the remaining heirs succumbed to accidental trauma. Pure business.'
inheritance.hargrove: Hargrove bows his head in shame: 'Forty-two years of service, young master, and dismissed with mere pennies in the draft will. I only wanted what my lifetime of labor earned.'
inheritance.odile: Odile weeps into her apron: 'My brothers were starving in the lower quarter, sir. The forged codicil would have bought our passage to America. Forgive me...'

cover_up.marika: Marika whispers in agony: 'I slipped the sedative into your father's tea so he wouldn't sign the transfer. I never meant for him to drive! When you woke up, I knew you'd remember.'
cover_up.elise: Elise shivers, tears breaking her composure: 'Father found out what I had done with the bank vaults. I gave him the drops to make him sleep. The crash was an accident, but you were remembering!'
cover_up.vance: Vance's voice is taut: 'A fatal medication error on my watch three months ago was covered up by your father. If your memory returned, my medical license and freedom were finished.'
cover_up.hargrove: Hargrove's hand trembles: 'I had borrowed from the safe, sir. The master had confronted me that evening. I only intended to induce slumber to replace the funds before dawn.'
cover_up.odile: Odile cowers against the wall: 'The master saw me taking the silver. He threatened the constables. I put the sleeping tonic into his flask so he would forget. I didn't mean to kill them!'

obsession.marika: Marika laughs with broken affection: 'Every picture, every diary, everyone who stood between us... I tore them away. You were mine in the hospital, and you will stay mine forever.'
obsession.elise: Elise's eyes burn with desperate intensity: 'You were the only person in this wretched family who ever cared for me! I ran the car off the road so you would never walk away again.'
obsession.vance: Nurse Vance steps forward, gaze unhinged: 'I nursed you through three hospitalizations. None of these parasites deserved you. You needed someone who truly understood your fragility.'
obsession.hargrove: Hargrove speaks with quiet madness: 'You are the only worthy scion of this bloodline, young master. The others were parasites dragging you down. I cleansed your path.'
obsession.odile: Odile clings to the photographs: 'You were the only one who saw me as human in this whole dark house! I couldn't let them take you away to the city. You had to stay here with me.'

swallowed_ending: The hairline cracks shatter into blinding light. Time collapses upon itself. Adrian's consciousness dissolves into the cold stone walls of the manor. The loop closes permanently.
victory_coda: In the hush that settles over the manor, a forgotten memory surfaces clearly: the melody Marika hummed on the balcony that rainy autumn morning before the world fractured.
